summary: Jan Rypka worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1905–1910) and held posts at Charles University in Prague (~1927–1958) and the University of Paris (~1946–1947).

Jan Safarewicz was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Vilnius University (PhD ~1922–1927) and in Paris under Émile Benveniste and Antoine Meillet (~1929–1931), later holding posts at Vilnius University and Jagiellonian University.

Jan Szczepan Otrębski specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Warsaw, Leipzig, and Jagiellonian University (PhD under Jan Michał Rozwadowski), and held posts at Vilnius University and Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań (1947–1960).

Jan T. Ergardt worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Lund University under Rune Edvin Arvid Johansson, earning his PhD by 1970, and was later affiliated with Lund University (attested 1989).

Jan Westerhoff works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Cambridge (PhD ~1999–2003 under Michael Potter) and SOAS (PhD ~2003–2007). He held posts at Oxford, Durham University (~2010–2013), and Lady Margaret Hall (~2015).
Jan Wilhelm Boissevain was an Indologist. He earned his PhD at Leiden University (~1900–1905) under the supervision of Jacob Samuel Speyer.

Jan Willem de Jong worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Leiden University (PhD under Jan Gonda and F. D. K. Bosch), Harvard, and Paris, later serving at Leiden (1950–1956) and Australian National University (1965–1986).

Jan de Vries specialized in linguistics, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1909–1915), studied under Willibald Kirfel, and attended Leiden University, where he later held a post from 1926 to 1946.

Jan van der Valk is a scholar of Tibetology and Indology. He earned an MSc at KU Leuven (2005–2010) and a PhD in anthropology at the University of Kent (2012–2016), later working as a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Vienna (2018–2024).

Jan-Ulrich Sobisch specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under David P. Jackson, David Seyfort Ruegg, and Nubpa Rinpoche, and held posts at the University of Hamburg, University of Munich, and University of Copenhagen (2003–2016).
Janakiballav Bhattacharyya worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied as a pupil under Surendranath Dasgupta and held a post at Jadavpur University (attested 1977).
Janardan Mishra specialized in Indology and philosophy. He served as Director at the Mithila Institute of Post-Graduate Studies and Research in Sanskrit Learning (attested in 1959 and 1987).
Jane Bunnag worked in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of London by 1969, studying under supervisors E. Michael Mendelson and Barbara E. Ward.
Jane Caple is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She has held posts at the University of Leeds and as a Research Fellow at the University of Manchester (attested 2026).

Jane Ellen Harrison specialized in religious studies and archaeology/history. She studied at Cheltenham Ladies' College and Newnham College, Cambridge, under Robert Alexander Neil, and held a post at the University of Cambridge (~1898–1922).

Jane Helen Rowlands worked in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Bangor University, Newnham College, Cambridge, the University of Calcutta (MA ~1924–1926), and the Sorbonne/University of Paris (PhD ~1928–1930), later teaching English at Karimganj College (~1952–1955).
Jane-Marie Law is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. She has held posts at Cornell University as Director of Graduate Studies (attested 2008) and Associate Professor (attested 2026).

Janet Gyatso is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her BA, MA, and PhD at UC Berkeley, holding posts at Stony Brook, Amherst College (1987–2001), and Harvard University as Hershey Professor of Buddhist Studies (from 2001).

Janet R. Goodwin works in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at UC Berkeley under Delmer M. Brown and Britten Dean, and held posts at the University of Southern California and the University of Aizu (both attested 1994).
Jang-Kil Chun is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Paul J. Griffiths, Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Frances Wilson, and doctoral supervisor Minoru Kiyota.
